Witness Structure: Dispatch for the Seawall

Socucius Ergalla has asked me to deliver a dispatch of recent immigration records to Herennius Varo at the Vivec branch of the Census and Excise Office. He says that the office is located in the Western Tower of the Seawall of Vivec.
I have delivered the dispatch to Herennius Varo at the Seawall Census and Excise Office. He paid me a courier's fee of 300 Septims for my services.
I refused to deliver a dispatch for Socucius Ergalla. He says it cannot wait and he will need to hire a courier service instead.
Witness Structure: Witnessed and Regarded

Ajira says she has heard stories of the Dreugh of the Seawall bestowing treasures upon "heroes of great will." It might be worth investigating these creatures if I ever have reason to travel to the Seawall.

A Land Dreugh at the Seawall of Vivec regarded me without hostility, then made a deliberate gesture, pointing toward the tidal pool. In the distance, ripples have formed across the water’s surface without any clear cause. I believe the Dreugh was turning my attention there...
A Dreugh in the tidal pool has gestured toward the depths of the waters. At its lowest point, the coral shifted and parted, revealing a passageway.

I found a massive Dreugh in the coral chambers beneath the Seawall. It regarded me in silence and then made a deliberate gesture toward an altar within the chamber. It was covered in valuable objects, left undisturbed. As far as I can tell, it seems that the Dreugh was gifting these many objects to me.
Witness Structure: Pilgrimage of the Wall
Danso Indules at the High Fane has asked me to complete the Pilgrimage of the Wall. I must gather a piece of Dreugh shell and leave it as an offering at the Shrine-Upon-the-Wall.
I have left an offering of Dreugh shell at the Shrine-Upon-the-Wall and have been granted a blessing.
Danso Indules was pleased that I was able to complete the Pilgrimage of the Wall. She has granted me a liturgical text on the Seawall as a token of appreciation.
Witness Structure: Measured Indulgence

I have heard that Selathu Trevayne, the Temple’s head cook at the Seawall, has been seen looking unsettled of late. It seems she carries some quiet frustration. Whatever troubles her is thought to be small in nature, yet important to her.
Selathu Trevayne, a Temple cook at the Seawall, appears to be upset over a crate of misplaced mazte.

Selathu Trevayne explained that a shipment of ten bottles of mazte meant for the kitchens never arrived. She does not know how or where the shipment was lost, only that its absence reflects poorly on the kitchens. She suggested I speak with Farvyn Sero at the Eastern Tower commissary, who is responsible for stores and supplies, to determine what happened to the misplaced mazte.

Farvyn Sero checked the commissary records and confirmed that the mazte never reached the Seawall. According to the ledgers, the shipment of ten bottles was meant to be received at the Elmas Island watchtower. No such delivery ever arrived there. Farvyn suspects the crate may have been misdelivered due to a misread address, and believes it could have ended up at Omani Manor, the only other significant holding on Elmas Island. I should inquire there and speak with whoever manages their stores.

Ranor Dralas admitted that Omani Manor received an overshipment of mazte, though he claims it was logged as manor property once it arrived. He is willing to release the ten bottles I need, but only if I pay him a 'processing fee' of 250 Septims

Ranor Dralas admitted that the shipment of mazte was misdelivered to Omani Manor and logged into their stores by mistake. He is willing to correct the records and release the ten bottles I need for a 'processing fee' of 50 Septims.

I’ve recovered the ten bottles of mazte that were meant for the Seawall kitchens. The shipment had been misdelivered to Omani Manor and logged into their stores, but Ranor Dralas has now released it to me. I should return the bottles to Selathu Trevayne at the Seawall as soon as possible.

I delivered ten bottles of mazte to Selathu Trevayne for the Temple kitchens at the Seawall. She cared little of how the bottles were obtained, only that the kitchens were properly supplied once more. I was given some fresh loaves of bread from the Temple kitchens as compensation.
Witness Structure: Turret Restorations

Battlemage Lucius Aelius, at the Western Tower turret of the Seawall, indicated he might welcome my help restoring the tower’s Daedric turret cannon. He says he will need written permission from General Viera Aurane before he can assign any tasks to me. I should speak with Aurane directly if I wish to continue.
General Aurane has granted me permission to assist Aelius with his project to restore the Western Tower's turret defenses. She gave me a letter bearing her seal to take back to him.

In order to restore the Daedric turret cannon, Lucius Aelius would like me to acquire a Daedric runestone of frost. He says they might occasionally be found in Daedric ruins or treasure hoards, though he did have a lead on one that is for sale. Apparently Miun-Gei, an enchanter in Vivec's Foreign Quarter, currently has such a stone available for purchase. Aelius gave me 300 Septims to cover expenses for the stone.
I have given a Daedric runestone of frost to Lucius Aelius. He was pleased, and was able to install it into the mechanisms of the tower turret immediately.

Lucius Aelius now needs me to acquire a Daedric runestone of shock. He did not have any specific leads on where one might be found, but he said I could try a small islet nearby. He says an old map of the Seawall shows that the islet south of the watchtower at the eastern end once held a small shrine to Sheogorath. He is not sure what remains of the shrine, but he said it's as good a place to start as any.

I have given a Daedric runestone of shock to Aelius. He was able to use the stone to complete his restorations of the Daedric turret cannon. As compensation, he provided me with an enchanted ring with abilities similar to those of the Seawall turret, though naturally less powerful.
Witness Structure: Borrowed Reflections

Crazy-Legs Arantamo has asked me to retrieve Saryth Drethan's Journal from his chambers at the Seawall for the Guild. Drethan is the Lord Commander of the Vivec's Seawall and a minor noble of House Indoril. Arantamo says a client is willing to pay well if we retrieve this item, but it's going to be a challenge. Apparently Drethan's chambers are constantly guarded by his retainer, Moryn Relas, and the client has strict instructions that Drethan and Relas are to remain alive.

Crazy-Legs Arantamo was very impressed that I managed to pull the job off. He paid me the client's full promised payment of 5000 drakes, and he threw in a few powerful tools as well, as a personal bonus.

Crazy-Legs Arantamo was not pleased to learn that Moryn Relas had been killed, but he was sympathetic that it was an incredibly difficult job. Arantamo says that the client certainly won't want anything to do with the journal now, but he still paid me 500 drakes out of his own pocket. He says he might be able to recoup some of the operational costs off the journal in a few years, when it isn't so hot.

Crazy-Legs Arantamo was displeased to learn that the Lord Commander had been killed. He says the client will be extremely upset and won't pay us anything now. He suggested that I lose the journal somewhere and forget the whole thing.

Saryth Drethan has given me the key to the Seawall's ancestral tomb and asked that I return it when I have finished my business. The tomb is located on the lowest level of the Eastern Tower of the Seawall.
I have returned the key to the Seawall tomb to Saryth Drethan.
Witness Structure: Final Interment
PLACEHOLDER

Rilos Delms at the St. Delyn Potter's Hall has asked me to retrieve the urn of his ancestor, Varothril Delms, from the ancestral tomb at the Seawall. He intends to re-inter all of his family's remains within the Ghostfence. He has given me a letter from the High Fane authorizing entry to the tomb for this purpose. I should present the letter to Saryth Drethan, the Lord Commander of the Seawall, to gain entry.

I returned to Rilos Delms with the urn of his ancestor. He asked me to carry it on the final leg of its journey to the Ghostfence, and I agreed. I am to deliver the urn to Uvoo Llaren at the Ghostgate Temple, who will see that the remains are reconsecrated directly into the Ghostfence.
Uvoo Llaren accepted the urn of Varothril Delms and informed me that the remains would be re-interred shortly. My work with Rilos Delms appears to be complete.
After returning to Rilos Delms, he asked me to take the urn to Ghostgate for him, but I told him I was too busy. He understood and paid me a Triune coin for retrieving the urn from the Seawall tomb.
It bears the private reflections of my Lord Indoril Drethan, and it is wholly improper that you would even consider asking me about such a thing. Now I have duties I must attend to. Leave me.

I apologize, Your Eminence, but even the Poet Himself has verse locked away in His Fane that He refuses the world. Each of us must have a private station for reflection, as I am certain you understand. I would gladly speak with you on the many wonders the Three have set before us, but my personal papers must remain where they belong. Locked within my desk in the proper and correct place.

It is a personal retreat where I may ponder and reflect upon a lifetime of service and duty... And it is very much private. Now, there are many things upon the Wall that must be seen to, and set aright, so unless there was a pertinent matter to bring to my attention, I suggest that we adjourn this conversation.
I'd prefer we never speak of that again, %PCRank.

The Lord Commander's dead?! B'vek this isn't good. The client will be extremely unhappy. At this point, we'll be lucky if they don't sic the Dark Brotherhood on us to keep us quiet. You're not out of the Guild. You're still the best damn thief we got. But I certainly can't pay anything for that journal anymore. I suggest you lose the thing... Preferably somewhere deep at the bottom of the bay. And you might want to lay low for a month... or a lifetime.
Pity how things turned out on that one. Let's not talk about it anymore.

Damn... The lapdog's dead, is he? Well, I knew this job was gonna be a tough one. Listen. The client won't want anything to do with this journal anymore, but I'll pay you some change out of my own pocket for the thing. You did as well as anyone might have, given the setup. I'll put it somewhere it won't be found, and maybe I can make up some of the operational costs in a few years. Ya know? When the thing isn't quite so hot.
I still can't believe you actually managed to pull that off. If I ever get a job that high-profile again... Well, I might retire off the profits. But I know I'm asking YOU to get it done for me.

You actually managed to do it, you crazy bastard. You got the damn thing without a hitch. Here, you've more than earned your share of the dragon's loot. And here: a few extra bits and bobs from me. Consider them a gift for a job well done. Now I'd still lay low for a few days. It's only a matter of hours before the Gold Masks catch on and no doubt they'll be on us and like shalks on a pomegranate. But take a few days off and enjoy them. You've more than earned a vacation.

Well, hey. I get it, %PCRank. These things take time. Everything worth anything in life is worth waiting a bit for. I'm patient, and the client is too, so long as the job gets done and it gets done right.

It's the journal of the Lord Commander of the Seawall, and we got a client who is willing to pay BIG for it. There's a catch, though. The journal's somewhere in his chambers and when the f'lah's not writing in it, it's gonna be under the careful watch of his lapdog, Moryn Relas. The client's got clear orders, see? Drethan and Relas are to remain unharmed. But you get that journal, %PCRank, and we all stand to make a lot of the Emperor's coin. I wouldn't ask anyone else. Get that journal for me, %PCName.
Again, I am pleased that you were able to complete your pilgrimage. You may leave an offering of Dreugh shell as often as you like to receive the shrine's blessing.

I am pleased that you have completed the Pilgrimage of the Wall. Here, please accept this Temple liturgical work on the Divine nature of the Seawall. Read it, and then perhaps you will understand why it is so important to our faith. It is a bit of an outdated text in terms of the current politics of the Wall, but it still contains an important lesson to bestow.
As I've said, you will need to gather a piece of Dreugh shell and leave it as an offering at the Shrine on the Seawall to complete this pilgrimage.

The Pilgrimage of the Wall will take you to the Shrine-Upon-the-Wall. The shrine stands near the middle of the Great Seawall, just to the southeast of here. Leave a piece of Dreugh shell as an offering at the shrine, and then read the inscription upon the shrine to receive its blessing. Return to me once you have completed this pilgrimage.

General Viera Aurane is the Champion of the Seawall Legion Garrison, and Varinia Pullo is her second-in-command. Battlemage Lucius Aelius is a recent addition here. He has been charged by General Aurane with the restoration of the Western Tower's Daedric cannon. Other than those Legion higher-ups, the main person of note would be Herennius Varo. He is the Chief Excise Officer down in the Imperial Census and Excise Office.

Indoril Saryth Drethan is the Lord Commander of the Seawall and the whole of the Seawall's Temple command answers to him. Moryn Relas is a minor retainer of Great House Indoril, and a loyal servant and confidant to the Lord Commander. Edras Flervu is the head Temple priest of the Seawall. Farvyn Sero is in charge of the Commissary, and Armiger Diram Velynth serves as the shrine attendant over at the Shrine-Upon-the-Wall.

Lord Indoril Saryth Drethan is the commander of the Seawall's Temple forces and can be found in the Eastern Tower of the Wall's Great Gatehouse. Viera Aurane commands the Wall's Legion Garrison and can be found over in the Western Tower.

The cannon serves its purpose. That is all you need to know. Its workings are not for idle inquiry, nor for those outside the Temple’s charge. If that Imperial battlemage sent you, you may return to him and report whatever you like. You will learn nothing of value here.

I am pleased to hear that you and Battlemage Aelius have restored the turret to full functionality. Vivec's defenses are stronger for it. You have proven yourself to be a true friend of the Legion and the Citizens of the Empire.

I was perplexed that the Imperial General who served in this post before me, simply left it atop the tower to sit in disrepair. I recently brought Aelius on to study and restore the device, and he has proven quite the talented artificer, restoring its basic functionality within mere weeks. Mind you, given the current peace, I do not intend to actually use it, but Vivec is one of the largest cities in the Empire. Should the need arise, I intend to defend it with every tool possible.
The cannon remains fully functional and operational, %PCName, in no small part thanks to your efforts.

The cannon accepted the runestone of frost with absolute ease. I am confident the cannon is completely ready to be restored to full functionality. All that remains is acquiring a final Daedric runestone.
I'll continue my calibrations on the cannon while you are away retrieving that Daedric runestone. With any luck, it should be ready to accept the new runestone as soon as you return.
Like I said, I'll need the written permission of General Viera Aurane if we are to continue discussing the Daedric turret cannon.
Yes, that's true. There is still quite a bit of calibration that needs to be done. Thanks for the moment of distraction, citizen, but you're right. I must return to my work.

Yes, actually. I could make good use of an extra set of hands to retrieve a few parts for me. But I'm afraid I cannot just accept anyone's help. I would need the General's written permission to bring anyone new onto this project. Go and speak with her if you're of the mind. I'll be here if she gives her go ahead.

Quite the contraption, isn't it? Not my own work, of course. Temple-make, through and through... Ancient engineering, and stubborn besides. I've been tasked by General Viera Aurane to restore its functionality. When the legion first leased the Western Tower, it was found to be completely defective. The Temple assured us the mechanism failed decades ago... though I confess I have my doubts about the full truth of that report. It seemed to accept the Daedric runestone you see in that alcove with ease.

To reach the shrine, take the gondola from the eastern docks of the High Fane to the Eastern Tower of the Seawall's Great Gatehouse. From the Seawall docks, make your way onto the Wall via a stairwell just to the east. Follow the Wall heading east through Guardhouse Seht. Continue along the Wall and just after it curves north, you will see the shrine on your left. I've also heard there are Imperial tour guides in Ebonheart who could give you more precise directions if you need.

The Shrine-Upon-the-Wall is directly to the southeast of here, located on the Great Seawall of Vivec. It honors an ancient compact that Lord Vivec forged with the Dreugh. From Temple canon on the matter, the Dreugh were the original architects of the Seawall. They constructed an elaborate fortress of coral around Vivec's palace, and aided the mightiest of Vivec's soldiers in repelling an invading Akaviri force.
No worries, %PCName. I have them ready if you change your mind.
Well then, please return when you have the coin. My tour services are, after all, a professional undertaking.
Here you are. One Guide to the Seawall. Enjoy.

Yes, it was a labor of no small effort that my sister and I put into this robust guide. I can sell you a copy for 10 drakes. It should prove most useful if you choose to navigate the Seawall on your own.
Best case: he never wants anything to do with the Guild again. But I can think of many worse cases...
He will be very happy we were able to pull this off, %PCRank.

I can't tell you who he is, for he prefers to remain very much anonymous, but I will tell ya, the mer has strong ties and allegiances within many different Imperial organizations. I don't know what he hopes to find in this Indoril lord's journal, and I don't really care. All I know is he is going to pay us big, and I mean BIG.

As the Western Tower's turret has been fully restored, your assignment here at the Seawall has now concluded. On behalf of the legion and the people of Vivec, I would like to thank you for your service, %PCRank.

As the Western Tower's turret has been fully restored, your assignment here at the Seawall has now concluded. On behalf of the legion and the people of Vivec, I would like to thank you for your service, %PCName.
I have already granted you my leave to assist Aelius with his turret restoration project. Do not fail me, %PCRank %PCName.
I have already granted you my leave to assist Aelius with his turret restoration project. Do not fail me, %PCName.

As General and Champion of the Seawall Imperial Garrison, I hereby grant you permission to assist in the restoration of the Western Tower's turret cannon. You are to report to Battlemage Lucius Aelius on this assignment. Here, take this letter bearing my seal to Aelius and he will set you to work right away. Serve the Empire and its citizens well as you carry out this task.

So, you've been speaking with Battlemage Aelius? He has requested your assistance in restoring the tower's turret, then? Well, you are a legionnaire in good standing, and if Aelius has requested your assistance, then I trust his judgment on the matter. Wait here just a moment.

So, you've been speaking with Battlemage Aelius? He has requested your assistance in restoring the tower's turret, then? Well, your reputation certainly precedes you, %PCName. I have heard good things about you and what you've done for the people of Morrowind. Wait here just a moment.

So, you've been speaking with Battlemage Aelius? He has requested your assistance in restoring the tower's turret, then? Well, to be frank, citizen, I have no idea who you are. If your reputation preceded you, or perhaps if you were in the legion yourself, then I could assign you to this task. As it stands, I have no idea who you are, and I cannot ask any of my comrades to vouch for you. I'm afraid I cannot entrust the Seawall's defenses to a complete stranger.

You've received the General's permission to assist me? Excellent! That is wonderful news. Well, I suppose we might as well just get to it then. As you can see in the alcove just over there, I was able to partially restore the turret with a Daedric runestone. Two more pedestals remain to accept additional stones. I am going to need you to retrieve a Daedric runestone of frost.

Standard Legion procedure. I'm sure you understand. You'll find General Aurane in her quarters just below the tower's winch room. Use the trap door to the winch room here, and then find another trap door in the winch room to the main corridors of the Western Tower. After climbing down the ladder, the General's quarters are the first door on the left.
Very well. Perhaps next time.
I'm afraid I cannot just distribute these maps free of charge. They do take quite a bit of effort to produce.
There you are. One Map of the Seawall. Please treat it well.

Yes, I am something of an amateur cartographer. I can sell you a Map of the Seawall and its surrounding environs for 25 drakes. It should aid you in navigating the Seawall's exterior, and it should make for a fine souvenir from your visit.
Thank you again for your assistance in this matter, %PCName. Your service to the Empire has not been forgotten.

And with that... it is done. The Western Tower's cannon is now fully operational. Thank you for your assistance in this matter, %PCName. Here, take this ring as compensation. I created its enchantment during an initial experiment to see if I could simply enchant the cannon directly. It is not nearly as powerful as the cannon itself, of course, but it should have a similar devastating effect, especially in close quarters.

You've managed to find a Daedric runestone of shock? That's excellent news, %PCName. Here, give it to me. The pedestal calibrations have already been completed and it should be ready to accept the final runestone.

You'll know a Daedric runestone of shock by the deep-purple crystal housed within. Check out that islet first since it is nearby. You'll find it just to the south of the southernmost tip of Elmas Island at the eastern end of the Seawall.

This one may prove more difficult. I do not have any solid leads on where one might be found. Your best bet is probably to search old Daedric ruins. I did discover something interesting that you could check out though. I found an old map of the regions surrounding the Seawall. Apparently, on a small islet south of the Elmas Island Watchtower, once stood a shrine to Sheogorath. I've not been to the islet myself, so I have no idea what remains of the shrine. It is as good of a place to start as any, though.

There. It has accepted the stone without issue. We shall be able to rain frost upon any enemy foolish enough to assail this fortress. Our work is not done yet though. We still need a Daedric runestone of shock.
Excellent. This is a fine example of a runestone. Hold a moment... I have just finished my intended calibrations of the pedestal. Let's see if it will accept this runestone outright.

I learned Miun-Gei had one for sale from contacts in the Vivec Mages Guild. You'll find Miun-Gei's shop in the Lower Waistworks of the Foreign Quarter of Vivec. If you find one anywhere else, I'll gladly accept it instead. The frost runestone variant is of similar construction to the flame one you see here, except that it holds a crystal of a deep-blue hue.

The cannon requires three runestones to stabilize the spell lattice. Without all three, the mechanism cannot channel its full power. The Daedric runestone I've already managed to install is a flame variant. I would like to acquire a frost variant, and I do have a lead on where one is to be found. I've learned that the Enchanter Miun-Gei has one for sale at his shop in the Foreign Quarter. Here, take these 300 drakes. They should be more than enough to cover the cost of the runestone and travel expenses.

They are quite rare these days. They were once used as ceremonial traps and defenses for the many Daedric shrines that dot Vvardenfell's landscape, however most of these have long since been looted by adventurers. Here at the Seawall they were repurposed to power the magical turret engines on the four main towers of the Seawall. The three turrets belonging to the Temple remain perfectly functional. Only the Western Tower's was malfunctioning, according to the official Temple report.

The Legion values reliability above all else. If something breaks, you fix it. If something works, you make sure it keeps working. That applies just as much to people as it does to equipment. I was brought here because the turret needed someone who could understand it and get it functioning again. I intend to see it done properly.

The Legion exists to hold the Empire together where distance and difference would otherwise pull it apart. That duty is not always clean, but it is necessary. My grandfather carried it before me, blade in hand, and I carry it still. Last Measure now rests at my side as it once did at his. It is a reminder that command is not to be taken lightly, and that service is not something set aside.

The Legion’s presence here is permitted under the terms of the Armistice. They are disciplined, but many of their officers do not understand the necessity of restraint within sacred bounds. I observe their conduct as is required, and maintain the limits of their authority as is expected. Cooperation is a matter of necessity, not of trust. It must be upheld with clarity.

The matter has already been handled and the records corrected. The mazte is no longer part of the manor’s stores, and there is nothing further for us to discuss on that subject. I trust it will not trouble either of us again.

Of course, %PCRank. I'm sorry that you have had to concern yourself with this matter. A shipment was misdelivered here and I recognized the error as soon as the records crossed my desk. It was logged into the manor’s stores before the mistake was caught, but that is no excuse. The mazte was never meant to remain here. I will see it released to you, and the ledger corrected in full. Please accept my apologies for the inconvenience, and my thanks for allowing this matter to be resolved quietly and cleanly.

Very well. This will suffice. I will amend the ledgers to reflect a clerical correction and authorize the release of the bottles to you. Consider the matter settled, and let us both agree that it is better when such minor irregularities are handled quietly and without unnecessary attention.

Then there is nothing further to discuss. The mazte will remain where it is. Properly logged and properly stored. If you change your mind, you know where to find me, but I won’t revisit the matter without compensation.
Yes? Have you reconsidered? My previous offer still stands.

The mazte... I had a feeling that might come up. There was an error in the delivery, I won’t deny that. The shipment arrived here when it was meant for another destination, and by the time the mistake was noticed it had already been entered into the manor’s stores. Once goods are logged, matters become... Complicated. Still, I see no reason this needs to become an issue between us. For a small processing fee of 50 Septims, I can correct the records and release the bottles to you without further trouble.

Mazte? Yes, I am aware that the manor received more bottles than originally expected. An overshipment. These things happen often enough when couriers are involved. Once goods are logged into the manor’s stores, however, they are treated as our responsibility, regardless of how they arrived. If you are asking to have the excess released, that would require revising the records and compensating the estate for the inconvenience. I would be willing to see that done for a processing fee of 250 drakes.

My apologies, %PCRank. I was not aware that such a matter was troubling you personally. If there has been any error regarding a shipment of mazte, it was certainly not intentional. I leave such logistical concerns to my steward, who oversees the manor’s stores and accounts. Please speak with Ranor Dralas and he will see the matter clarified for you at once.

If you have come to trouble me over a crate of saltrice spirits, then you have badly misjudged how my time is to be spent. I do not involve myself in such trifles, nor do I account for every bottle that enters my household. If there has been some confusion or misdelivery, you may take it up with my steward, Ranor. He handles such matters, and I suggest you direct your bothersome questions to him and not me.

If some shipment has gone missing, you’ll need to speak with Councilor Omani’s steward. Ranor Dralas oversees all household accounts and inventories, and he’s the one who would know more about such matters.

I’ve heard the kitchens are properly stocked again. That means the ledgers can remain closed, which is always preferable. However the matter was resolved, it no longer concerns the commissary, and I’m satisfied to leave it at that.
I've already consulted my records on that particular shipment. I'm afraid I have no other information on the matter. Was there something else I can assist you with today?

Here it is. This particular shipment was routed by land, not sea. It was to be received at the Elmas Island watchtower, at the eastern end of the Wall. No such delivery arrived. I suspect the most likely possibility is that it may be an error of a misread address. The only other holding of note on Elmas Island is Omani Manor. It is possible the crate ended up there. You would do well to inquire with the Omani Manor staff. Speak with whoever keeps their stores.

Mazte? Yes, I am aware of the allotment you’re referring to. Ten bottles, bound for the Temple kitchens. They have not passed through the Seawall’s commissary, nor were they received dockside. If the shipment was sent, and I have no reason to believe it was not, then it failed to reach its final leg. Wait a moment. Let me consult the commissary ledger.
The kitchens are settled again. Mistress Selathu is no longer displeased. That is good. Thank you.

Those bottles... Are they the ones meant for the kitchens? If they are given to Mistress Selathu, that will be good. When the stores are whole, questions stop being asked. I would be glad to see this matter finished.

The mazte did not come to the kitchens, no. Mistress Selathu was... displeased. When things go missing, it is often the cooks who are questioned first, or the hands that carry the crates. I have accounted for all stores that reached the hearth. If the bottles are found elsewhere, then perhaps the fault will not rest here. It would be good if they were returned soon.
The kitchens are supplied again, and that is all that matters. The bottles are accounted for, and the Wall is better for it.

These will suffice. Ten bottles, as recorded. I care little how they were found, only that they are here now. The kitchens will answer no more for their absence, and the Wall keeps its natural order. You have done what was asked. Please, take these. Five loaves of scuttle-stuffed saltrice bread. They are of my own making, prepared for long nights and empty stomachs. They are a hearty meal and keep well. You have done a service to the Wall, whether you intended to or not. Go, and may Almsivi go with you.

As far as I have seen, nothing has changed regarding this matter. Ten bottles were approved and did not arrive. Until they are returned, the kitchens must answer for their absence. If you have made no progress, then there is nothing more for me to say.

When it is absent, the fault reflects upon the kitchens, and therefore upon me. If the mazte has simply been misplaced rather than stolen, then it will be found by those whose duty it is to track such things. If you wish to be of help, speak with Farvyn Sero at the commissary here in the Eastern Tower. He oversees the stores and supplies of the Wall. I require only that the bottles be returned.

Ten bottles were expected. No more, no less. They were recorded and approved properly, and allotted for the kitchen stores as part of the small Temple allowance of spirits here. They did not arrive. I am not an Ordinator, but I serve them faithfully. The small measure of wine they are permitted is not indulgence. It is discipline, observed with restraint.

This urn contains the remains of Varothril Delms? I was expecting this. Thank you for delivering this here. I will see that it is interred in the proper ossuary under Lord Vivec's watch according to his descendant's wishes. I shall also see that the ancestral mages reconsecrate the deceased's spirit directly into the Ghostfence. Three Blessings upon you, sera.

You wish to enter the Seawall's ancestral tomb to retrieve these remains? Such a request is highly irregular. Yet this letter bears the seal of the High Fane, and their authority is not mine to question. Here. You will return this key to me once your business is concluded. The tomb is on the lowest level of the tower. Enter, retrieve the urn, and depart. Disturb neither the offerings nor the other remains. The tomb is not unattended. Ancestral guardians keep watch there. Proceed with care and reverence.

Under no circumstance will I permit an outlander so vile as the one before me to enter the sacred hall of the dead in my keeping. If these seals are legitimate, then Rilos Delms himself, or a priest of the High Fane, may come to retrieve the remains. You will not... Leave my presence at once.
I am pleased to hear that the urn arrived at Ghostgate. Let no Dunmer say the Delms Clan did not give itself in service to the people of Morrowind.
Please take the urn to the Ghostgate Temple. No need to hurry back once you have done so, but I would be glad to see you again here at the Potter's Hall in the days to come.

I understand, %PCName. Here... I'm afraid I am quite the poor man, and do not have much to pay you, but take this triune coin for your services in retrieving the urn. I shall arrange for another courier to transport these final remains to the Ghostfence. Thank you again for all your help.

Thank you, %PCName. I am a poor man, so I cannot pay you much. Still... take these ten triune coins I had set aside to pay a courier. And for all that you've done, take this as well: One of my finer pieces. Now please get that urn to Uvoo Llaren at the Ghostgate Temple. She will see that it is interred in the same ossuary as the rest of Delms clan. May the Poet guide your path, friend.
I am glad that you have returned here with the urn. Tell me, %PCName. Would you be willing to assist me further? Do you think that you could take the urn on the final leg of its journey to Ghostgate?

The easiest way to reach the Eastern Tower of the Seawall is to take a gondola from the High Fane. When you enter the tomb, find the altar bearing the seal of Great House Redoran. Varothril was a minor retainer of that house, and thus should be found with the other retainers. I will await for you to return here with the urn of Varothril. Thank you again for agreeing to this solemn task, %PCName.
Very well, %PCName. I understand. I will be here if you change your mind.

Thank you, %PCName. My work here at the Potter's Hall keeps me quite busy, so I'm afraid I have little time to leave the canton. Here, take this letter. It is a document bearing the seal of the High Fane, authorizing the exhumation of Varothril Delms for the purposes of re-interment. Present that letter to the Lord Commander of the Seawall, Saryth Drethan, and he should grant you access to the tomb. He will be found at the Eastern Tower of the Wall's Great Gatehouse.

Varothril Delms is the oldest ancestor of my lineage recorded in the archives of the High Fane. He was a stonemason who perished in the construction of the Seawall of Vivec, and thus was given burial within the Wall's own tomb. He gave his life in the raising of one wall, so it is only fitting that his bones now help guard Vvardenfell once more. I would see the whole of the Delms clan reunited, including myself when I am called, and given unto the Ghostfence. Would you be able to assist me?

You stand now in the Western Tower of the Seawall of Vivec. The Western Tower is under perpetual lease by the High Fane to the Empire, and hosts an Imperial Legion Garrison, the Vivec Census and Excise Office, and various other support services. Across the gatehouse canal, stands the Eastern Tower. There you will find the Seawall Temple command and services. Beyond that, the Seawall stretches east toward the Dreugh Colony and Elmas Island.

The Eastern Tower hosts the Temple command for the entirety of the Seawall. Just to the west is the Western Tower, which under allowance from the High Fane of Vivec, is currently occupied by the Imperial Legion. To the northeast of here is a sacred tidal pool, host to a clan of Dreugh loyal to Lord Vivec. Just above the pool stands the Shrine-Upon-the-Wall. And near the eastern end of the Wall are the Towers of Vehk and Veloth, along with the Elmas Island Watchtower.
This is the Tower of Vehk of the Seawall. To the west of here lies the Shrine-Upon-the-Wall and the the Great Gatehouse. To the east is the Tower of Veloth and Elmas Island.

Lord Commander Drethan is a man of principle, and one who understands the weight of his station. We do not always share perspective, but I do believe that we share purpose, even if he would disagree. He maintains the Temple’s authority with precision, and I respect that. Our cooperation is not born of convenience, but of requirement and of mutual understanding. The Wall stands because both sides know where their duty begins, and where it ends.

My lord has perished, and his murderer simply stands before me as if nothing had occurred. I have forgotten my place... There is no path forward save vengeance. I shall reach heaven by violence, just as the true Lord of this Wall has taught me.

You will refer to my liege lord as Lord Indoril Drethan. If you have cause to speak with him, you will address him as serjo, and you will be conscientious, concise, and courteous. If you have any difficulty in remembering these simple directives, you will answer personally to me.
He's dead. I've already forgotten about him. I suggest you do the same.
Lord Commander of Vehk’s big wall and all that Temple brass. Always keeps his nose buried in duty and his quill scratching away in some journal. Well... not so much anymore. Lucky for us.

The f'lah's the so-called Lord Commander of Vehk's big wall. Guess he's some big-shot Indoril from the Mainland as well. Lord Commander of the Seawall is more or less one of the only posts of any note that the Indoril maintain here on the Black Isle. Basically, the guy's important. Remember that while you go rummaging through his drawers.

Saryth Drethan is Lord Commander of the Seawall and a minor noble of Great House Indoril. He largely keeps to himself from what I understand, though all the Temple Dunmer of the Seawall speak of him with high regard. If you need to speak with him, he'll be found across the gatehouse canal, within his chambers in the upper levels of the Eastern Tower.

Indoril Saryth Drethan is the Lord Commander of the Seawall of Vivec, and all Ordinators stationed here answer to his authority. He is a mer of long service and steady judgment. The Watch has been kept in good order under his command. If you have reason to speak with him, he'll be found in his chambers. They are just above the upper level of the Ordinator quarters, near the ladder to the tower's winch room.

Indoril Saryth Drethan is the Lord Commander of the Seawall of Vivec, and all Ordinators stationed here answer to his authority. He is a mer of long service and steady judgment. The Watch has been kept in good order under his command. Some say the Seawall is a lonely post for one of his standing, but Lord Drethan holds that duty carried out in the sight of Vivec is no small honor.

Ajira has heard curious stories about the Dreugh that dwell beneath the Seawall. Some say they reward heroes of great will with treasures from their coral halls. Ajira does not know if such stories are true... but the Dreugh are clever creatures. Perhaps they can sense strength of mind. Or perhaps they are simply fooled by powerful magic. Ajira wonders which.

Have you noticed Selathu Trevayne lately? She's the head of the Temple kitchens, here at the Seawall. She keeps her temper well enough, but she’s been pacing the kitchens like something’s gone missing. If it were the Wall's stone, or something equally grand, she'd speak plainly. Since she hasn’t... I’d wager it’s something small that matters greatly to her.

House Indoril does not seek prominence. It fulfills its obligations. We stand closest to the Temple because all other Houses have forgotten what is required of them. We bear the weight without complaint. Service is not distinction. It is burden. Those who carry it properly do so without question, just as God taught us at Kummu.

Great House Indoril stands in closest accord with the Tribunal and bears the weight of that proximity without complaint. Our duties are not matters of preference, but of obligation, shaped by doctrine and history, and upheld through discipline. Authority is not taken, but maintained through proper conduct and adherence to the will of the Three. To serve House Indoril is to serve the Temple, and to do so without deviation or indulgence.

Dreugh shell is the traditional offering to leave at the Shrine-Upon-the-Wall. Just as the Wall protects Vivec, the shell protects the Dreugh who serve Lord Vivec and the Seawall. Dreugh shells are gathered from slain Dreugh, but most alchemists and apothecaries here in Vivec will sell them as well.

Dreugh shell is the traditional offering to leave at the Shrine-Upon-the-Wall. Just as the Wall protects Vivec, the shell protects the Dreugh who serve Lord Vivec and the Seawall. Dreugh shells are gathered from slain Dreugh, but most alchemists and apothecaries here in Vivec will sell them as well. You could also try searching the waters of the sacred tidal pool, just below the shrine. I would ask you not to harm the Dreugh there, but you may be able to find shed pieces of their shells on the seafloor.

General Aurane is a distinguished legionnaire, and more importantly, a practical one. She understands when to push and when to leave things as they are. That’s not always easy to manage here. She gave me the clearance I needed to work on the turret, though from what I’ve gathered, not all within the Temple are pleased with that decision. But she’s been clear about expectations from the start. I respect that. It makes my work a good deal easier than it might otherwise be.

General Aurane is a capable officer, and her conduct reflects an understanding of the boundaries set by Lord Vivec's Armistice. She serves the Empire with discipline, as I serve the Temple. Our purposes differ, but where they must align, they do so as required by our respective lords. I neither question her authority within its proper scope, nor permit it to extend beyond what has been granted.

Last Measure was my grandfather’s blade, and now it is passed to me. It has seen more service than I have, and likely more than I ever will. It is not a symbol of office or authority. It is a reminder of what is expected of me. The blade belongs where it is needed... and for now, that is here, at the Seawall.
Care for a trip to the Seawall? It's just a short journey south over the water via gondola.
I can take you by gondola to the Great Gatehouse docks.
I can ferry you across the canal to the Western Tower, out to the Eastern Gatehouse docks, or north to Vivec's High Fane.
For a few drakes, I can take you across the gatehouse canal in my gondola to the Eastern Tower.

Are you ready to conclude the tour, %PCRace? We can head out to the terminus of the Wall on Elmas Island, or if you prefer, we can head back now in the direction of the Great Gatehouse docks or return to Ebonheart.
Our tours make brief rest stops at the Seawall Great Gatehouse docks, the Shrine-Upon-the-Wall, and then conclude on Elmas Island.

Omani Manor can be found on Elmas Island, just north of the eastern end of the Seawall. Follow the Wall east until you reach the watchtower at its far end, then exit down the ramp onto the island below. Once you are on Elmas Island, follow the path to the north. The manor is not far, and there are no other structures on the island you might mistake it for.
You'll find him in the commissary. It's the first door on the left when you exit the canteen, back into the main corridors of the Eastern Tower.

Moryn is the most loyal companion and retainer an Indoril could hope to have. He has served me faithfully and diligently for many years, and his devotion has never faltered. But that is all I would say of him to a stranger.
He's dead. I guess the dog can't do much guarding or lap sitting anymore.

He's the guard dog of this f'lah, Drethan. No doubt when he isn't guarding his Seawall Lord's life, he's guarding whatever treasure he's got stashed over there. He's a highly skilled warrior from what I have heard, and a bit of a religious fanatic, to boot. Best watch yourself around him.

He is a retainer of Great House Indoril, and a highly talented warrior. He is the personal guardian and man-servant of Lord Commander Indoril Drethan. He will almost always be found by his lord's side here at the Seawall.

*The Dreugh Lord rises to meet you, its presence vast and unmoving. A low, resonant sound issues forth. Not speech, but something carried with purpose. It does not advance. Instead, one great limb lifts, slow and certain, and turns toward the center of the chamber. There, an altar stands, laden with objects of age and value, undisturbed. The Dreugh Lord holds its gesture, offering what lies upon it.*

*The Dreugh regards you in stillness, its eyes fixed with intent. A low, rasping sound escapes it. Not speech, but something measured. One limb rises, slow and deliberate, and turns toward the depths. Below, the coral shifts. The living reef parts at the pool’s lowest point, revealing a passage where none stood before. The Dreugh holds its gesture... indicating the opening below.*

*The Dreugh does not recoil. It stills, its gaze fixed upon you with deliberate attention. Slowly, it raises a claw and makes a measured gesture. Once, then again. Far off, the surface of the tidal pool begins to stir. Ripples form without wind or current, spreading in careful, unnatural patterns. The Dreugh turns slightly, and points toward the distant ripples.*
You have concluded your business in the tomb. Very well. I will take the key and see it returned to its proper place.
Conclude your business in the tomb and return the key to me. Until then, we have nothing further to discuss.
Welcome to the Chapel of Talos, my child. Feel free to rest here a while, and reflect upon whatever you wish. Whether you come in faith or simple curiosity, all are welcome here.
My lord... He is... slain...

You approach the private chambers of Lord Indoril Drethan. You will conduct yourself with discipline and restraint. Speak only if you have cause, and do so with clarity. My lord does not suffer idle petitioners. If you have no matters of substance to bring before him, I will not permit you to trouble him.
State your purpose. If it concerns my lord, speak clearly.
You stand in the presence of Lord Vivec. Keep your voice low, and your purpose clear.
If you’ve come with a purpose, speak it. If not, I suggest you find one quickly.
You stand within an active Legion Garrison. Conduct yourself accordingly. Now... What is it you require?
I am General Viera Aurane. If you have business at the Seawall, state it plainly and I will see it addressed.
You are received. Be concise, and speak only to matters that warrant my attention.
State your business, sera. The Wall does not suffer idle words, and neither do I.
You stand within the Seawall. Conduct yourself accordingly. Speak if you must, but do so with purpose.
Isn't this place just splendid? And those views... You can even see the Ebon Tower from here!
Please, friend. Not now. My wife and I are trying to enjoy the tour.
Yes, %PCRace? I hope you are enjoying the tour.
...Shortly, we'll be headed northeast to the Tower of Vehk. It is still a fair journey there, so I invite you all to take a moment to rest and enjoy the splendid views.

...In the waters below the wall, sit the remnants of the Dreugh colony who still honor this compact. They are quite docile compared to other members of their ilk, though it would still be wise not to approach them too closely. Their presence here has largely stumped modern scholars. Some claim they are driven by divine compulsion, while others...

...And here, we have now arrived at the Shrine-Upon-the-Wall. Dozens of pilgrims make the trek here daily to leave offerings of Dreugh shell. The shrine commemorates an ancient pact forged between the Dark Elven god, Vivec, and the mythical kings of the Dreugh. If you look closely at this stonework...
Hail, traveler! Would you care to join us for a tour of the Seawall today?
The Dreugh keep the Wall and the Shrine. Compact and faith compel them onward, as they do all others.
The Shrine stands inviolate, blessed by Living God and Trident Lord alike.
Walk upright and with purpose, just as Vehk of Ald Resdayn.
Vivec stands whole: God and City as one. Neither diminishes the other, nor stands apart.
The Seawall watches all upon it, and all around it, and all beneath it.

Patriarch %PCName! I am deeply humbled by your presence in our humble hall. I know it may be far above my station to trouble you with such matters, but I would ask a moment of your time if you would grant it. Would you hear an old potter's plight?
Greetings, %PCRace. You are a servant of the Temple, are you not? There is a small matter in which I could use the aid of one who serves Vivec. Would you care to listen to an old potter's plight?
Greetings, %PCRace. You know... you seem like the trustworthy type. Would you care to listen to an old potter's plight?
How goes the search for a Daedric runestone of shock?
Have you acquired a Daedric runestone of frost for me yet?
I'd really appreciate your help in restoring the cannon, but like I said: I'll need the General's permission before we continue.
Hail traveler. Admiring the Daedric turret cannon, I see...

Hey, %PCRank. I got a job for you. You're one of the best damn thieves we got, so if anyone can pull this one off, it's you. We've been tasked by a high-profile client to steal Saryth Drethan's journal.

You look new to the Wall. If you’ve come seeking quiet or certainty, you’ll find little of either here. But I’ve a practical concern instead. A crate of misplaced mazte that should already be warming the tables under regimented Temple allowance. It is a small thing, perhaps, but small things weigh heavily when one is charged with keeping the Watch fed and hearty.

Yes, yes... I'm afraid I'm quite busy at the moment. We are expecting quite the volley of merchant vessels to transit through the Great Gate today, and they don't inspect themselves now, do they? What's that? Ah, yes... I see... You're here with that dispatch from Ergalla then.

You know, %PCName, you've proven yourself to be quite the reliable sort. Would you like to do a bit more work for the Census and Excise Office? I need someone to deliver a dispatch to our office in Vivec.
You know, %PCName, you do seem to be quite the trustworthy sort. Would you like to do a bit of work for the Census and Excise Office? I need someone to deliver a dispatch to our office in Vivec.
How fairs your pilgrimage, %PCRank.

Greetings, %PCRank %PCName. In recognition of your current standing within the Temple, we would now ask that you undertake a new pilgrimage right here in Vivec City. I would ask for you to complete the Pilgrimage of the Wall.
Greetings, traveler. Is there anything I can get for you?
Yes? Can I get ya anything?
Hail, %PCRace. Welcome to the Mess Hall. Finest establishment this side of the Seawall! Anything I can get for ya?

You wonder to find a Dunmer priest of Talos, and in Vivec's sacred city, of all places? Well... I was born in Narsis and raised in the traditions of the Tribunal. I carried that faith with me into Cyrodiil, though distance has a way of changing how one understands what they were given. It was there that I first encountered the worship of Talos, not as opposition, but as something strangely familiar. In time, I chose to serve Him... though I have not forgotten where my faith began.

I was trained as a battlemage in the Imperial tradition, though I’ve always had more interest in how things function than in how they’re used in combat. That inclination has a way of following you through your career. I’ve served in a few different postings, mostly where my skills were needed to assess or repair arcane devices. The Seawall is easily the most unusual assignment I’ve had.

I am Moryn Relas, retainer of House Indoril and sworn servant to Lord Indoril Drethan. My duty is singular. I stand where I have been placed, and I act as required. Skill at arms is expected, not praised. Loyalty is not spoken of... it is demonstrated. I have served my lord for many years, and I will continue to do so without deviation.

I was born in the Nibenean Heartland and raised in a household where service to the Empire was expected, not chosen. My grandfather served as a legionnaire before me, and I was taught early that rank is not privilege, but obligation. I have served in several postings across Cyrodiil and Morrowind, but the Seawall is unlike any other. Here, discipline alone is not enough. One must also understand restraint.

I am Saryth Drethan of House Indoril and the anointed Lord Commander of the Seawall. I am charged with its care in accordance with Temple authority. My service is not one of ambition, but of obligation, inherited through House and sanctified by duty. I have stood this post for many years, and in that time I have learned that vigilance is not an act, but a condition to be maintained without lapse.

Ebonheart serves as the Empire’s anchor in Vvardenfell, a place where authority is established in clear terms. It is orderly, direct, and predictable. The Seawall is none of those things. Here, every action carries the weight of consequence. I serve Ebonheart and maintain a presence there when required, but my duty lies here. The Wall demands more attention than any court or council ever could.

Mother is the Queen of Morrowind, and Her will is expressed through the protection and guidance of the faithful. Strength, when properly guided, preserves what must endure. Those who serve the Temple do so under Her gaze. To act without regard for that is to invite correction.

Clockwork is the architect of hidden order, and His designs are not meant to be understood by all. That does not lessen their necessity. Structure exists whether it is seen or not. Those who serve within it are expected to recognize their place, even if they cannot perceive the whole. To question that place is to misunderstand it.

Selvia Kvinchal is the cook and publican for the Mess Hall. She can serve you a drink or meal, though don't expect much else from her. Draccus Vircutian is the Legion smith, and he sells standard Legion kit, as well as a few imported bits from the West. Finally, dockside you'll find the Chapel of Talos. Severyn Drelayne is the Imperial Cult Chaplain for the Seawall Garrison, and offers basic healing and apothecary services.

Selathu Trevayne is head cook of the Temple kitchens and can provide meals for pilgrims and travelers alike. Farvyn Sero is chief of the Temple Commissary, and keeps a small number of provisions available for purchase. Vedryn Arano is the Temple Master-at-Arms and head of the Ordinator training hall. The only other service of note here in the Eastern Tower is the small Tribunal shrine, just outside the Ordinator barracks.

The vast majority of the services available here at the Seawall will be found over in the Great Gatehouse. Temple services are to be found in the Eastern Tower, and Imperial Services are housed in the Western Tower.
Yes, yes... Thank you again for your service to the Imperial Census and Excise Office. Now please, excuse me.

Yes, I've been expecting this. Let me see that immigration dispatch... Yes, everything looks to be in order here. With all the ships through today, I'll probably need Dirvanye to enter these into the records for me. By the Nine, she'll be thrilled about that... Here take these 300 drakes for services rendered. Thank you for your assistance in this matter.
What's this? An immigration dispatch? That'll be meant for Agent Varo, not me. He's up front, behind the counter.
I'm sorry, %PCName, but I have already prepared the document to be sent via courier. I'm afraid there is no task I need assistance with right now.
Yes, I had heard from Herennius Varo that he received that dispatch in a recent correspondence. Thank you again for all of the assistance you have provided to the Census and Excise Office.
Yes, please do get that dispatch to Agent Varo at the Seawall. It is not highly urgent, but it must be completed.

Thank you, %PCName. I need you to get that dispatch to Agent Herennius Varo at the Vivec Census and Excise Office. The office is housed in the lowest level of the Western Tower of the Seawall of Vivec, right next to the canal docks by the Seawall's Great Gate. Varo is expecting this document, so he will pay your courier's fee upon receipt of the document. No need to return to me afterwards. He will notify me in a future correspondence.

There is no need to be rude, %PCName. Well, it is what it is. I'm afraid I cannot wait around too long to get this dispatch sent out as it is overdue already. I shall prepare to hire a courier service to get the document delivered to the Seawall. Farewell.

No? Well, it is what it is. I'm afraid I cannot wait around too long to get this dispatch sent out as it is overdue already. I shall prepare to hire a courier service to get the document delivered to the Seawall. Farewell, %PCName.

Yes, I need someone to deliver a dispatch of recent immigration records. Not a high priority, but we do need to send these sorts of documents to our partner offices from time-to-time to maintain accurate records. So what do you say, %PCName? Would you be willing to do this small service?

It’s a strange post, the Seawall. Quiet most days... quieter than a place like this ought to be. You start to notice things after a while. The way the water moves. The way the Dreugh gather below the surface. The way even the veterans keep their voices low when they’re on watch. Makes you feel like you’re standing somewhere you’re not meant to be.

The Seawall is a sanctum of purpose, not spectacle. It stands as a bulwark, yes, but also as a reminder that all things must remain in their proper place. The faithful walk its length in reverence, while others pass through it without understanding. That distinction is not for the Wall to enforce... but it is always observed.

The Seawall is a place of boundaries and contradictions, much like Vivec Himself. Here, the Temple and the Empire stand beside one another. It is an uneasy balance at times, but also a meaningful one. I have come to see the Wall as a kind of lesson... that differing truths may still endure in the same place, if they are held with care.

The Seawall does its job well enough. It’s defensible, well maintained, and far more complex than it appears at a glance. There are mechanisms here that don’t quite match the official accounts regarding their functions. I’ve learned to take most reports here with a measure of caution. What’s written down and what’s actually in front of you don’t always line up.

The Seawall stands because it was set in its place by God, and because those who serve Him understand what must be preserved. It is not merely defended... it is maintained through vigilance and obedience. The Temple holds it in trust, and are the only ones worthy of its stewardship, save the divine.

The Seawall is both a fortification and a line that must not be crossed lightly. It protects both Vivec and Ebonheart, yes, but it also marks the boundary between Temple authority and Imperial responsibility. The arrangement is delicate, but it holds. My duty is to ensure that the Western Tower remains secure and operational, without disrupting the order maintained by the Temple along the rest of the Wall.

Though it serves the role well, the Seawall is not merely a fortification. It is a structure of doctrine, set in stone to endure and to witness. It stands where coral once arose at Vivec’s command, and remains as testament to that covenant. It does not act without cause, nor yield without reason. All who pass upon it are measured in quiet ways. It exists not to assert itself, but to remain, as all things properly ordered must.

The Seawall is an ancient structure. It predates the Septim Empire, though scholars disagree on the exact timeframe in which it was built. Temple records claim it was constructed in its current form during the early Second Era, though many Imperial historians have placed its architectural style as a much later construction.

The Seawall of Vivec is an incredible sight if you have not seen it before. It is the largest fortification on all of Vvardenfell, save the Ghostfence. My sister, Vinissia, and I offer a tour service to see its many splendid vistas.

The Seawall does not simply protect, nor does it merely enclose... It witnesses. It stands in its proper place and receives all things as they are: tide, oath, passing life. Nothing is hidden from it, for it endures where others do not. To walk upon it is to be seen... and to become, in some small way, part of what it remembers.
I never really understood why we needed a Seawall here in the first place. Isn't that what this city's got its own God-King for? Protection? I guess it's pretty, I suppose.

I mean, it's south of Vivec. It's hard to miss the thing. But I suppose you just want directions. You can grab a gondola from the Temple, or you can just walk to the place by heading south from Ebonheart. I know Drethan's somewhere in the Eastern Tower, but I've got no real idea where he's holed up in all that. It's your job to case the joint when you get over there. Good luck, %PCName.

The Seawall is south of Vivec and encloses the entirety of Norvayn Bay. To reach the Western Tower of the Seawall, start at Ebonheart. Head south from the dockside plaza there, crossing the bridge onto the large island south of town. The Western Tower of the Seawall is located at the southernmost point of that island. The road between Ebonheart and the Seawall is poorly developed, so you'll need to follow a rough track of land through the countryside.
The Seawall is south of Vivec and encloses the entirety of Norvayn Bay. The Vivec branch of the Census and Excise Office is located there, housed within the Imperial administered Western Tower.

Our office controls the flow of maritime trade into the Norvayn via the Seawall's Great Gate. We perform inspections of the merchant vessels that pass through, and from time to time we process new immigrants to Vvardenfell. However, most of the immigration traffic is diverted to our partner office in Seyda Neen. Due to the limited number of gates along the Wall, we prefer ships do not stop at our docks for too long, so as to not impede the flow of traffic.

The Seawall is obviously a grand and formidable military structure, but it is also much more than that. It is a holy site. A grand temple of the Warrior-Poet in its own right. Walk with caution and reverence whenever you tread upon its battlements.

The Seawall is the principal naval fortification for both the City of Vivec and the Norvayn heartland of the Ascadian Isles. When Vvardenfell was opened to settlers, a provision was entered into the Armistice that established a joint command structure for the Seawall. The Western Tower is under Legion jurisdiction, and the eastern portions of the Wall remain under the purview of the Temple.

The Seawall is an ancient and monumental naval fortification, but like all the works of Lord Vivec, it is first and foremost, a holy site. There are a half dozen or so shrines and pilgrimage sites along its length, and a pilgrimage to the Wall is considered a sacred undertaking.
You are standing now on the Seawall, of course. It is an ancient and sacred structure. Remember that as you walk its length.

The Temple is not merely doctrine, nor only devotion. It is the ordering of the world as it ought to be. Here upon the Seawall, that order must be maintained with particular care. There are influences present that do not share in our understanding, yet must still be accounted for. Faith alone is not sufficient. It must be upheld through vigilance.

I'm still surprised that the Archcanon assented to the Legion lease on this place. Perhaps he knows something we do not... or perhaps the yearly tithe carried more weight in the High Fane’s decision than they would care to admit. The Temple keeps a tight hold on the Seawall. Their records are thorough, but not always complete, and what they choose to leave unsaid is often just as important. Still, for its age, they’ve preserved the Wall remarkably well. I’ll give them that.

The Temple is not an abstraction. It is an order... a structure... made visible and enforced through those who serve it. Faith without discipline is weakness. Doctrine without action is meaningless. Here, both are upheld. Those who walk the Seawall will understand that... whether they believe it or not.

The Temple governs more than faith here in Vivec... It governs structure, expectation, and the conduct of those who serve under it. I have found its authority to be consistent, even when its methods differ from our own. The Seawall is not a place where the Legion can impose itself freely. We operate within bounds, and those bounds exist for a reason. It is not my place to challenge them without cause.

The Temple is not merely an institution, but the structure through which the proper order of Morrowind is maintained. Its authority is not derived from consensus, but from the will of Almsivi, made manifest through doctrine and practice. Here upon the Seawall, that authority is observed in full. All things are kept in their proper place, and it is my charge to ensure that this remains so, without compromise.

Watch them, if you would understand. Not their form, but their motion. They do not waste it. They do not move without purpose. When they turn, when they pause, when they offer. These are not idle things. The tide carries meaning, for those with the will to receive it.
Yes, you have already listened to my plight. Thank you.

I am the last of my line here on Vvardenfell, and I have no intention of having children of my own so late in life. I do, however, want to ensure that the Delms' family legacy lives on in some small way. I have been preparing to have all of my family's remains re-interred into the Ghostfence. Most of their remains have been gathered already from the tombs here in St. Delyn and sent ahead. However, one more set is yet to be sent: the remains of Varothril Delms.

The Shrine is not a mere place of offering... It is a place of accord. Here, what was sworn is remembered, and what endures is set in its proper place. The tide does not disturb it, nor does the false dragon diminish it. To stand here is to be made aware... and to remember what must not be forgotten.

Vivec is a god who remains present within the world. His teachings are not distant or abstract, but lived and observed. He stands in relation to His people, bearing both authority and consequence. That kind of divinity carries weight, for certain. That is something that I came to understand more fully only after I had left it behind. It is not lesser than other forms, only different in its expression.

God does not require belief to exert His will. The Wall stands because He willed it, and it endures because that will is maintained through proper conduct. Those who serve here do so within that design. Whether they understand it is of little consequence. What matters is that they do not disrupt it.

Vivec is not a presence the Legion can afford to misunderstand. This city, the Wall, and the people who live in its shadow are shaped by His will in ways that cannot be ignored. I do not claim to serve Him as the Temple does, but I do recognize the order He has established here. It is not my role to question that order... only to ensure that the Empire does not disrupt it without cause.

Lord Vivec is the foundation upon which all here stands. The Wall, the compact, and the order it preserves are extensions of His will, set into the world that they may endure beyond any single age. He does not compel through force or show of strength, but through the proper arrangement of all things. To serve here is to stand within that arrangement, and to uphold it without deviation.

Vivec is divided, and whole. God and City, warrior and poet... Each face speaks, yet all are one truth. He does not dwell within the world; the world is arranged around His will. To know Vivec is not to understand Him... but to stand where He has taught, and endure.

Talos represents a form of divine completion. Where the Tribunal remain within the world they shaped, Tiber Septim became something that moved through it without being bound to it. His presence is not tied to place, but to continuity... to the unfolding of history itself. I serve Him now, but I do not see that service as a rejection of what came before. Only a continuation along a new path.

There are no beds for travelers or pilgrims here in the Eastern Tower. There is a small rest area you may make use of at the Shrine-Upon-the-Wall, northeast of here. Otherwise, you can take a gondola from the docks here back to the High Fane and stay at one of the many fine inns in the city proper.

I got no beds for rent, I'm afraid... If you're with the Legion, just head upstairs and grab a bunk in the barracks. Otherwise you're gonna have to make the trek north back to Ebonheart and rent a room with Agning at the Fishes.

Vehk is the motion within stillness... The hand that writes and the hand that strikes. The one whom the Webspinner anticipated. The sigil of two and one score. He teaches not by command, but by example set within contradiction. To follow Him is not to imitate, but to hold one's place with purpose. To act when it is required.
I trust you are enjoying the tour. If you have any questions, you need only ask.

Yes. My sister and I offer a guided tour service along the Seawall of Vivec. It is a magnificent monument and a sight no visitor to Vivec should miss. I can also sell you a Guide to the Seawall or a Map of the Seawall if you prefer a more self-guided experience.
